## Natural history notes

A small sack-bearer moth characterized by tan to brown wings with scalloped darker lines, rounded wing margins, and a soft, leaf-like resting appearance. In Florida, the Scalloped Sack-bearer Moth is found in wooded and semi-wooded habitats such as hammocks, forest edges, pine flatwoods, parks, and yards where suitable shrubs and trees occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars live in portable silk cases or “sacks” covered with bits of plant material, feeding on foliage and sheltering inside the case for protection.
